review_note: Drafted 2026-11-04 from the native enrollment test fixture (AddTransactionPolicies) and marked for owner review. Owner direction 2026-11-04: zero means no limit and no limit is the proper default for the transaction lifetime, snapshot age, active-transaction count, lock count, lock memory, wait-graph size and deadlock work (Firebird design; every attached user is always in a snapshot transaction). The remaining values are still the fixture's choice; these policies are to be monitored in live operation.
review_flags: Superseded 2026-11-04: the drafts were 64 concurrent transactions, 60-second transaction and snapshot lifetimes, and a 256-lock / 64 KiB lock table with a 128-node, 256-edge, 4096-work deadlock graph. All are now 0 (no limit).

deadlock_detection_interval_microseconds 100000 and fairness_threshold_microseconds 1000000 are not limits and remain the fixture's choice; the detection interval default is an open owner question (Firebird detects deadlocks on conflict; its 10 s DeadlockTimeout only drives the dead-owner purge).
Only two isolation profiles are declared (read_committed_statement and maintenance_operation); SBsql surfaces more isolation levels than this.
